abstract.text: Follow a report from the shake on the device to the fix you install the next day.

inlineContent.text: ScreenClipKit only captures. Routing, the agent, the pull request, and merging all happen in ScreenClip on the Mac, the same way they do for a capture made on the Mac.
A shake, or
Report

on the banner after a system screenshot, takes a snapshot of your app’s own windows. The status bar, system alerts, and other apps are not included. The report sheet opens in its own window above your app, so your view hierarchy, navigation, and SwiftUI state are never touched.
The tester can draw arrows, rectangles, ellipses, freehand lines, and text, and redact anything private. Then they write a note and tap
Send
. Only the marked-up image leaves the device: annotations and redactions are burned in, and no unredacted copy is kept.

To report something seen earlier, the tester can tap the photo button and pick one of the device’s screenshots instead of the live capture. It keeps the device’s rounded corners when its size matches this screen and is otherwise scaled to fit it, and the report tells the agent it was picked from Photos, when it was taken, and that it may show an older build than the one installed. The live screen’s view tree is left out of its diagnostics. No photo library permission is needed: the system picker only shares the image the tester chooses.

Reports are sent only to a Mac the device has paired with. Pairing compares a 6-digit code on both screens, and every report is encrypted for that Mac.
ScreenClip files the report in the project whose
App bundle IDs

list your app. If no project lists it, ScreenClip looks for the bundle ID in each project’s Xcode settings. The report carries the device, OS, app version and build, and the visible screen. It also carries any
the tester chose to attach. The
Agent for iOS reports
setting chooses which agent works on it.

abstract.text: Report what you see in your own iOS app, straight into ScreenClip on your Mac, where a coding agent fixes it.
The optional files ScreenClipKit attaches, and how the tester controls them.
Starts ScreenClip: listens for the triggers, and reconnects to the paired Mac whenever the app becomes active.
Add ScreenClipKit to the Debug build of your app, pair a device with your Mac, and send a first report.
